Mean Vector of a Multivariate Gaussian

Source: R/mvgaussian_distrib.R
mv_location.MvGaussianDistrib.Rd

Returns the mean vector \(\mu\), which for this family is the first \(p\) parameters read off theta in order. The method is mv_leading_location(), shared with every multivariate family whose location is its leading parameters, so the gaussian adds nothing of its own here: \(\mu\) is both the location the density is centered on and the expectation of the law, which is not true of every family.

Arguments

distrib

An MvGaussianDistrib object, from mvgaussian1_distrib().

theta

A named list of parameters, one number each. Only the \(p\) mean components are read.

Value

A numeric vector of length \(p\), named v1, ..., vp after the coordinates of the response. The parameter names mu1, ..., mup do not appear on it.

See also

mean.MvGaussianDistrib(), which returns the same vector as the expectation of the law, mv_sigma.MvGaussianDistrib() for the matrix, and mv_location() for the generic.

Examples

d <- mvgaussian1_distrib(3)
theta <- as.list(stats::setNames(c(1, -2, 0.5, rep(0, 6)), d@params))

mv_location(d, theta)
#>   v1   v2   v3 
#>  1.0 -2.0  0.5 

# For a gaussian the location is also the expectation, so the two agree.
all.equal(unname(mv_location(d, theta)), unname(mean(d, theta)))
#> [1] TRUE
